transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. whatever comes back to you about the dream, just start wherever feels right.
it started snowing inside the office. no one else looked up.
snow falling indoors and nobody notices... that's odd. do you remember what happened next?
yeah it settled on the desks and keyboards, and after a while the whole place was white. you could only see the tops of the monitors.
it sounds strangely calm, everything buried in white while people keep working. what did you do?
i just sat there. it felt peaceful. then my manager dele came over to tell me something, and while he was talking he turned into a snowman. still in his blue suit.
a snowman in a blue suit, still talking to you... did it feel funny or was it normal in the dream?
it didn’t feel funny. it was normal somehow. he was still holding his coffee mug.
a snowman holding a coffee mug, and that's just how it was. what happened after that?
i made a snowball and it sort of glowed a little in my hand. then i woke up.
a glowing snowball in your hand. that moment right before you woke... do you remember if you were about to throw it, or just holding it?
i was just holding it. i don’t remember thinking about throwing it.
just holding it then. and the whole dream was you in it, or were you watching yourself from somewhere else?
i was in it. i was at my own desk, same as any day.
heavy, quiet, cold, none of those?
not heavy. more soft and watery, like a watercolour painting with the colours running into each other.
so everything felt a bit blurred at the edges, colours bleeding together. was there any colour that stood out most?
mostly whites and greys. dele’s blue suit stood out until he turned. then even that was sort of dull.
all that white and grey, and only the blue suit had any colour... did anything in the dream feel like it mattered to keep, or was it all just there?
the glowing snowball felt like the part that mattered. like the whole thing had been leading to it.

so you were at your own desk in the office, same as any day, and it started snowing inside. nobody else looked up, and the snow settled everywhere until the whole place was white, just the tops of monitors showing. it felt peaceful. then dele came over to tell you something and turned into a snowman still in his blue suit and holding his coffee mug, which felt normal. you made a snowball that glowed a little in your hand, and then you woke up. everything looked soft and watery, like a watercolour with colours running into each other, mostly whites and greys, and the glowing snowball felt like what it was all leading to.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
you got it right. all of it.
would you like to see it drawn?
yes i would

here are a few ways it could be drawn: a soft watercolour, soft and watery like a memory just out of focus. or pale coloured pencil on grey paper, gentle and detailed with an odd calm in the ordinary. or white and grey with a little blue, like an old photograph, quiet and real as if caught in a snapshot that never quite developed. or the way it looked as something real, like a literal camera but with the calm of a dream remembered clearly.

which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
soft watercolour, soft and watery like a memory just out of focus. that’s the one.

watercolour it is. i'll start with dele.

i picture him as an adult in his blue suit. i don't have more than that since you didn't say, so those are my guesses. would you change anything about him, or should i just go with that?
go with that

alright, dele stays just like that.

bright from outside, or softer because of the snow?
softer because of the snow

okay, softer because of the snow. i'm sketching the manager, dele and the coffee mug and the snowball now, and it'll appear on the right. nothing else is being drawn yet.

for the office, i picture a typical indoor office space with desks and monitors, including your own desk. there are keyboards and computer monitors, and the light is soft and even, like indoor light. these are my guesses, so tell me if anything's different, or should i just go with that?
go with that

okay, i'm sketching the office now and it'll appear on the right. nothing else is being drawn yet.

would you like to be drawn as yourself, if you tell me a little about you? or just as i imagine you?
just as you imagine me

okay, i'll draw you as i imagine you. nothing else is being drawn yet.

what colour did the snowball glow?
it was a soft white, but warmer than the snow around it.
does it look the way you remember?
it looks right.

good. i'll keep going.

want me to draw dele next?
yeah, go ahead.
okay, i'm drawing dele now. it'll appear on the right.
ok
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each carrying on from the ones before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
alright

the snow starting inside the office is on the right now.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah. no one’s looking up, they’re all just typing.

no one looking up makes it feel even more like a dream.

i'll draw the snow settling next, the whole office white with just the tops of the monitors showing.
ok
does it look the way you remember?
it does. only the tops of the screens showing, everything else buried.

nice, that's exactly how you described it.

the rest are still being drawn, they'll show up on the right as they're ready.
ok

the moment with you making the snowball, it glowing a little in your hand, is up on the right now. that's the one you said you'd pause on.

does it look the way you saw it?
it looks right. just holding it, the way it was.

i'm glad it looks right. one of the moments couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side, and i'm sorry about that.

thank you for sharing this dream with me. you can look through everything that's there on the right.
